walkthroughs.body_html:
Mechanisms — a core area of GCSE Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Mechanisms brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Mechanisms.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A 20-tooth driver gear meshes with a 60-tooth driven gear. What happens to the output speed?
options: It is reduced to one third of the input speed
It triples
It stays the same
It stops completely

mcqs.q: A wheelbarrow, with the load between the wheel and the handles, is which class of lever?
options: Second class
First class
Third class
It is not a lever

mcqs.q: A crank and slider converts which types of motion?
options: Rotary to reciprocating motion
Linear to oscillating motion
Reciprocating to oscillating motion
Rotary to rotary at right angles

mcqs.q: Two meshed spur gears rotate in which directions?
options: Opposite directions
The same direction
Random directions
They cannot rotate when meshed

mcqs.q: If a machine gives a mechanical advantage of 5, do you get force for nothing?
options: Mechanical advantage means the machine uses less electricity.
Machines multiply force without any trade-off, giving free extra work.
No — the force is multiplied by 5 but the effort must move roughly five times further than the load; work output never exceeds work input, and friction wastes some.
Lever classes are decided by the material the lever is made from.

mcqs.q: Does a larger driven gear make the output spin faster?
options: No — a driven gear larger than the driver turns more slowly, by the ratio of the teeth, but delivers more torque; a smaller driven gear spins faster with less torque.
Mechanical advantage means the machine uses less electricity.
Bigger gears always rotate faster because they are more powerful.
Gear size only affects how loudly the gearbox runs.

mcqs.q: In which class of lever is the load between the fulcrum and the effort?
options: Lever classes are decided by the material the lever is made from.
A wheelbarrow is a first-class lever because it is the most common example.
Mechanical advantage means the machine uses less electricity.
A second-class lever, such as a wheelbarrow; first-class levers have the fulcrum in the middle, and third-class levers have the effort in the middle.
